Following up on our renewal window — thanks again for the heads up on budget timing. Per our last call, Nexa is planning to double the dedicated footprint from 16 → 32 GPUs at the next term. I attached a first-pass pricing workbook that shows 12- and 24-month reserved rates and the incremental per-hour pricing for the additional 16 GPUs.

A few items we need to nail down to finalize the amendment:
- Desired contract term (12 vs 24 months) — this affects the per-hour reserved rate and renewal incentives.
- Target go-live for the expanded pool (start of next billing cycle or mid-term?).
- Throughput/latency SLO you'd like guaranteed for the larger pool (we can offer a per-route 99th p90 latency commitment + credits).
- Any required procurement language or PO workflow (Sasha / procurement email cc'd).

I've looped in Karthik (SE) to help confirm the throughput guarantees and sizing assumptions. If it's helpful, I can convert the workbook to a PDF and prepare a clean amendment for signature once we land on term and rate.

Vanessa,

Thanks for the note and the workbook — skimmed it this morning. A few procurement / finance questions before we schedule legal review:
1) Can you confirm the per-hour reserved rate for the incremental 16 GPUs as a single line item (not blended)? Our CFO needs that to model cloud runrate.
2) Is the discounted per-hour fixed for the entire term or only the committed-months?
3) What is the SLA credit formula if the throughput SLO is missed (we prefer a credit cap and a clear calculation).
4) We will likely prefer a 24-month term, but need your best rate for 24 months and the rate for 12 months for comparison.

Procurement asks that any amendment include our standard termination-for-convenience language; I can circulate a redline once we have the numbers. Budget approval target is Dec 15, so if we can get a signed amendment that week we'd be in good shape.

Also happy to do a 30-min call — Wed morning (PST) works for me.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Pricing knobs and throughput guarantees for Nexa 16→32

Vanessa / Marcus — quick internal note ahead of Wed call.

Assumptions I used in the workbook:
- Baseline: Nexa currently on 16 GPUs reserved, sustained median utilization ~65%, peak bursts up to 95% for 3–4 hours/day.
- Target: add 16 GPUs to create a 32-GPU reserved pool; recommend we keep their pool co-located in us-west-2 to avoid cross-region latency.

Pricing recommendations to be competitive but protect margins:
- 24-month commit: incremental 16 GPUs at $2.35/hr per GPU (reserved rate)
- 12-month commit: incremental 16 GPUs at $2.75/hr per GPU (reserved rate)
- Blended / temporary burst hours billed at on-demand 1.6x reserved rate if they exceed the reserved pool.

SLO proposal (what we can guarantee):
- Throughput: 99th percentile per-request latency <= 220ms for standard generation routes under steady-state.
- Credits: If 99th > target for the month, provide a pro-rata credit up to 10% of that month’s reserved spend.

Notes / negotiation levers: extended payment terms (net 60) and a 24-month commit give us room to lower the rate by ~15% vs 12-month. If they insist on termination-for-convenience, propose a 90-day notice with a pro-rated exit fee equal to remaining committed reserved hours at 40% of list.

I can join the Wed call to walk the SLO technical tradeoffs.

-Karthik
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@nexahealth.com>, Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@nexahealth.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — reserved pool expansion (16→32 GPUs)

Hi Liam / Sasha — thanks for the quick reply. Per Karthik's note (copied), here's a concise pricing summary you can share with finance/procurement:

Revised proposal (incremental 16 GPUs) — per-hour reserved rates:
- 24-month term: $2.35 / GPU-hour
- 12-month term: $2.75 / GPU-hour
- Burst / overage: on-demand multiplier 1.6x reserved rate

SLA / credits:
- 99th percentile latency target: <= 220ms (per-route, standard gen).
- If monthly 99th > 220ms, credit = prorated % of monthly reserved spend, capped at 10%.

Other commercial terms:
- Pro-rated start: amendment effective first day of next billing cycle unless otherwise requested.
- If termination-for-convenience required, propose 90-day notice + 40% remaining-commitment exit fee.
- Preferred payment term: net 30; we can consider net 60 with an early-pay credit.

Attached is a cleaned proposal PDF (v2) and a one-page amendment summary you can forward to procurement. I booked Wed 12/03 10:30 PST for a 30-min sync — confirm if that still works and I'll send the calendar invite.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Vanessa — thanks, the numbers look reasonable. A couple of quick asks from our side before the legal team starts redlines:
1) Can you add a clause that allows Nexa a one-time 30-day pro-rated failover to on-demand capacity in the case of planned maintenance of the reserved zone? (We need explicit language for our DR runbook.)
2) For the credit calculation, can you provide the exact formula in the amendment (monthly 99th latency vs target => credit percent = (excess_ms / target_ms) * alpha, capped at 10%) — our legal wants math written out.
3) DocuSign link for the amendment when it's ready — procurement prefers e-sign.

We are leaning to 24 months but will confirm on Wed's call. If the DocuSign link and the amendment text are available within 48 hours after the call, procurement can likely push to get signature by Dec 15.

Regards,
Sasha Patel
